content.comment_body: This is my first post here, so please be patient. I've built a remote boiler monitoring panel using a [product_name] and a [product_name] communication module. In case of a boiler failure alarm, the communication module should send an SMS to designated staff to notify them of the issue in the boiler area. The project went smoothly after a few initial challenges, mostly related to limited experience with [product_name] and especially the communication module. The module successfully sends texts every time we simulate or experience a real boiler fault. However, we are also receiving unexpected texts every 2.5 to 3 hours with a message like "IPv4#10.176.28.25"—the last digits change with each text. For reference, I've attached a screenshot. I understand this is related to some communication protocol, but I'm unsure what's triggering it or how to prevent it, as we can't fully implement the SMS feature until it is resolved. I've tested different ethernet cables to rule out connection issues, but nothing has changed. I also reviewed all online options in the communication module, but didn't notice anything obvious. Any advice would be greatly appreciated. Kind regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], I haven't personally used a [product_name] communication module, so I can't offer direct insight on that device. However, is it possible that a network component between the communication module and the phone (such as a router or VPN) negotiates a new IP address every 2.5 to 3 hours? Your screenshot seems to suggest this might be happening. Regards, [user_name] (translated by Google)

Hi [user_name], Thank you for your quick reply about my issue. I've managed to identify the cause. In the contacts section of the [product_name] communication module, there are two checkboxes next to each contact for "IPV4" and "IPV6" notifications. Both options were enabled for the test numbers I used, which resulted in a text message every few hours displaying a different IP address for accessing the communication module from a phone. Until now, I'd only used a [product_name] programming device with an ethernet cable and wasn't aware of this functionality. Essentially, if these boxes are checked, the contact gets administrator privileges to access and modify the communication module settings remotely. Thanks again for your assistance. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered unexpected SMS messages from the communication module displaying IPv4 address details every few hours, which interrupted the intended alarm notifications. Upon investigation, they discovered configuration options within the module were responsible, highlighting how unclear notification settings can lead to confusion. Initial project setup issues were mainly due to inexperience with both the main device and the communication module, with overlooked configuration choices adding to the complexity.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the communication module to send SMS alerts only when genuine boiler faults occur, not unsolicited protocol-related messages. Ideally, SMS features should be straightforward to configure, making notification settings evident and easy to adjust.
